facts: The reflecting surface spans 100 by 110 metres as an off-axis portion of a 208-metre parent paraboloid. The Gregorian subreflector is 8 metres across. The track is at 807.43 metres NAVD88.

record: NRAO geodetic survey and reference geometry
facts: The antenna azimuth/elevation axis intersection is the documented phase center with elevation axle 48.22 metres above the track. The surveyed reference location is 79°50′23.406″ W and 38°25′59.236″ N.

record: NRAO installed antenna and azimuth track record
facts: The final telescope uses a 64-metre azimuth track and saw first light in August 2000.

record: NRAO GBT active surface engineering record
facts: The approximately 485-foot height applies to the full structure. The active surface uses 2,004 reflector panels.
